title: TensorFlow LSTM Forecast with BigQuery
description:
A Google Cloud variant: sales, weather and holiday data live in Google BigQuery, a small TensorFlow/Keras LSTM predicts the next 7 days of demand per product and store, and an HTTP function (Cloud Run functions) serves forecasts and writes them back to BigQuery for dashboards in Looker Studio.

  • Parameterized BigQuery SQL builds one row per day (units, price, temperature, holiday); missing days count as zero sales.
  • The LSTM reads the last 28 days and outputs 7 days at once; the forecast band is the 10th to 90th percentile of validation errors.
  • Training reports the model's MAPE next to a seasonal-naive baseline (same weekday last week).
  • An optional step recommends a price from the 7-day forecast, stock and a price corridor.

The example trains on synthetic data on CPU; BigQuery is mocked in the tests.
implementationSteps: Create BigQuery tables for daily sales, stores, weather, holidays and a demand_forecasts output table.
Load 28+ days of history per SKU/store with a parameterized query and fill days without sales with zero.
Add day-of-week features (sine/cosine) and standardize all features on the training period.
Cut the series into 28-day input windows with 7-day targets and keep the last 8 weeks for validation.
Train a Keras LSTM(32) with MAE loss and early stopping; compare validation MAPE with the seasonal-naive baseline.
Save the model (.keras) with scaling parameters and error percentiles, and deploy it with the HTTP function.
On each request, read the last 28 days from BigQuery, forecast 7 days, append the rows to demand_forecasts and return JSON.
Optionally pass price, cost, stock and competitor price to get a price recommendation for the horizon.
Build a Looker Studio report on demand_forecasts and retrain on a schedule.
performance:
Targets, not measured results:

  • 30-day MAPE around 12 % is a common goal for stable, high-volume products; slow movers will be worse.
  • The model should beat the seasonal-naive baseline on a hold-out period; on the example's synthetic data it does (checked in the tests).
  • Training one SKU/store on two years of daily data takes seconds on a CPU; the HTTP function scales with request volume.
userExperience: Planners open a Looker Studio report that shows the 7-day forecast with its band next to actual sales. Pricing tools call one HTTP endpoint with SKU and store (plus optional price inputs) and get the forecast and a recommended price with the allowed range. Each training run prints how the model compares with the simple baseline, so teams can see where it adds value.
